operator: hostapd 2.11 and dnsmasq 2.92 in an OrbStack Ubuntu 26.04.1 arm64 VM; the console owner added the test networks and ran Test Connection

console.model_source: owner manual confirmation; PTP DeviceInfo reports the generic model 'Nintendo Switch'
console.firmware_observation_note: The console was not enumerated during this test; the firmware value is the owner's report.
console.modification_source: owner report; this test does not detect modifications

connection.upstream: none; the test AP had no NAT or internet forwarding

open.expected_failure_reason: The test AP had no NAT or upstream route, so the TCP SYN received no response.

wpa2.handshake: hostapd sent 1/4 and 3/4; the log records 'pairwise key handshake completed (RSN)' and authorized=1
wpa2.expected_failure_reason: The test AP had no NAT or upstream route.

ipv6.observed: The console sent IPv6 router solicitations to ff02::2.
ipv6.note: This is a precondition observation for Phase 5, not an IPv6 test.

capture.open_pcap: local-only; captured ARP, DHCP, DNS, ICMPv6 router solicitation, and the TCP SYN to the resolved Akamai address
capture.eapol_visibility: EAPOL frames were not visible on the AP interface because hostapd consumed them; the handshake evidence is the hostapd debug log
capture.management_attribution: hostapd -dd log and the console's own Test Connection behavior

phase1.console_state: Two test networks were added for the baseline. The owner was asked to remove them after the D10 work; no other console setting was changed.

commands.command: sudo hostapd -dd <open-ap.conf>; sudo dnsmasq --no-daemon --log-queries --log-dhcp; sudo tcpdump -i <interface> -w <local.pcap>
commands.result: TX10LED-NET reached AP-ENABLED on channel 1. The console associated with AID 1, obtained 192.168.77.94 over DHCP, queried ctest.cdn.nintendo.net, and attempted TCP port 80. Test Connection reported 2110-3128.

commands.command: sudo hostapd -dd <wpa2-ap.conf>; sudo dnsmasq --no-daemon --log-queries --log-dhcp; sudo tcpdump -i <interface> -w <local.pcap>
commands.result: TX10LED-WPA2 reached AP-ENABLED on channel 1. The console completed the WPA2 pairwise handshake, was authorized, obtained 192.168.77.94 over DHCP, queried ctest.cdn.nintendo.net, and reported 2110-3128.

commands.command: sudo kill <hostapd/dnsmasq/tcpdump>; sudo ip addr del 192.168.77.1/24 dev <interface>; restore managed mode
commands.result: The AP, DHCP/DNS server, and capture were stopped; the test address was removed; the adapter was restored to managed mode. The raw pcaps and logs remain local-only.

interpretation: Phase 1 reached the console's ordinary network stack on both the open and WPA2 test APs. The WPA2 pairwise handshake completed and the console obtained a DHCP lease and issued the connectivity-test DNS query. The Test Connection failure is explained by the deliberate absence of NAT or an upstream route: the console's TCP SYN to the resolved Akamai address had no responder. This is a valid baseline for association, DHCP, and DNS, not a parser or vulnerability result. The IPv6 router solicitation shows the console is willing to use IPv6 if a router advertisement is offered, which is relevant to Phase 5.
authorization: The owner approved Phase 1. The owner added the two test SSIDs, connected the console, and ran Test Connection once per SSID. No malformed frame, crafted DHCP/DNS/IPv6/TLS response, or other active test was sent.
limitations: No NAT or upstream route was provided, so Test Connection could not reach the TLS endpoint and failed at the internet step.
One console, one adapter, one driver, and channel 1 only.
The console's error code is recorded as displayed; its internal cause was not independently decoded.
EAPOL frames were not visible on the AP interface; the WPA2 handshake evidence comes from hostapd's debug log.
The two test networks remain saved on the console until the owner removes them.
The console firmware value is owner-reported; it was not re-read during this test.
This baseline does not test any parser, malformed input, or exploitability.
redactions: Console and adapter MAC addresses redacted.
Interface name redacted because it is derived from the adapter MAC.
